components.criterion: The view reads from below the standing subject rather than eye-level or above, through the underside of the chin and overhead bench/roof geometry.
components.evidence: The front boot dominates the lower foreground, the metal bench underside occupies the right half, and a narrow jaw-to-neck underside is visible beneath the chin; these co-visible planes make the apparent viewpoint lower than the standing torso.

components.criterion: Upward-facing projection includes overhead roof ribs and a clear view of architectural undersides.
components.evidence: Roof ribs and glass canopy extend across the upper frame above the actor. The bench bottom and structural underside are exposed from below in the right midground, rather than a tabletop viewed from above.

components.criterion: Nearby boots/lower body are visibly enlarged relative to the receding upper body/head in the same connected subject.
components.evidence: The nearest boot is a long enlarged foreground mass at bottom-left, with trouser legs receding upward to the smaller head; the rear boot reads smaller and farther away in the same connected stance.

components.criterion: Multiple vertical iron columns recede and converge toward the upper frame; this is coherent spatial perspective, not isolated leaning props.
components.evidence: The tall perimeter stanchion at left and the rear stanchion beside the head lean inward through the rising frame with narrowing separation at higher elevations; roof ribs continue the upward recession. The connected supports provide multiple perspective cues rather than a rolled frame alone.

camera_position_claim: Apparent relative position and projection only; actual camera height and focal length are not measurable from the saved image.

confusion_boundary_review.level_portrait_only: ruled_out by below-bench projection and overhead ribs
confusion_boundary_review.wide_lens_only: ruled_out by connected upward projection cues
